content.text: {"assessments":[{"evidence_id":"EV073","decision":"exclude","span_ids":["S3","S4","S6"],"role":"cross-system background","claim":"A different photocatalytic system in neutral water with TEOA reportedly produced mainly formaldehyde, with CO and CH4 as minor products.","transfer_limit":"Not a Co(II)–bipyridine comparison, different catalyst/platform, products, and medium; only broad background on TEOA-containing CO2 photoreduction. CO here is carbon monoxide, not cobalt.","reason":"Contains experimental observations with TEOA and product distribution, but the catalyst identity and reaction context are unrelated to the target Co(II)–bipyridine TEA/TEOA comparison, so it is too indirect for inclusion.","scores":{"research_relevance":1,"direct_evidence":2,"discriminatory_value":1,"transferability":1}},{"evidence_id":"EV074","decision":"exclude","span_ids":["S9","S10"],"role":"irrelevant","claim":"This snippet describes a copper gas-diffusion electrochemical flow-cell setup measured at room temperature.","transfer_limit":"Electroreduction on copper GDEs is outside the photocatalytic Co(II)–bipyridine TEA/TEOA scope.","reason":"No relevant photocatalytic Co-bipyridine, TEA/TEOA comparison, or transferable mechanistic observation for the stated question.","scores":{"research_relevance":0,"direct_evidence":1,"discriminatory_value":0,"transferability":0}},{"evidence_id":"EV075","decision":"include","span_ids":["S4","S5","S6"],"role":"system option / component evidence","claim":"A visible-light CO2 photoreduction formulation is explicitly reported that contains a Ru(bpy)3 photosensitizer, TEOA sacrificial donor, MeCN, and a cobalt-containing catalyst platform under high-purity CO2/Ar handling.","transfer_limit":"Catalyst is Co-Co LDH/MXene rather than a molecular Co(II)–bipyridine complex; snippet gives composition but not comparative TEA data or outcomes here.","reason":"Useful because it documents a fully specified TEOA-containing photocatalytic formulation with bpy-based photosensitizer and cobalt catalyst components, informing feasible comparator design and component accounting even though it is not the target molecular system.","scores":{"research_relevance":2,"direct_evidence":2,"discriminatory_value":1,"transferability":2}},{"evidence_id":"EV076","decision":"include","span_ids":["S2","S7","S8"],"role":"transferable characterization method evidence","claim":"XAS is described as element-specific, operable in situ/operando, and EXAFS can provide coordination numbers and interatomic distances, while XPS can identify surface composition and valence-state variations.","transfer_limit":"Method guidance is from single-atom catalyst context, not specifically a homogeneous Co(II)–bipyridine photocatalytic solution; adaptation to the target system requires validation of sample state and sensitivity.","reason":"Relevant as transferable characterization evidence for testing changes in cobalt coordination or valence under reaction conditions, which could discriminate donor-dependent speciation hypotheses in the target system.","scores":{"research_relevance":2,"direct_evidence":1,"discriminatory_value":2,"transferability":2}},{"evidence_id":"EV077","decision":"include","span_ids":["S2","S6","S8"],"role":"transferable mechanistic/method evidence","claim":"In a Ru–Fe photocatalytic system, the presence of Fe caused luminescence quenching consistent with photoinduced electron transfer, and a solution with TEOA was subjected to deoxygenation and 468 nm illumination cycles.","transfer_limit":"Different reaction chemistry (oxidation, Ru–Fe system, O2 atmosphere variable) and no TEA comparator; transfer is limited to using photophysical quenching and donor-containing illuminated cycles as mechanistic probes.","reason":"Provides direct example that luminescence quenching can report productive electron transfer in a donor-containing photocatalytic molecular system, which is useful for designing discriminating measurements in the Co(II)–bipyridine context.","scores":{"research_relevance":2,"direct_evidence":2,"discriminatory_value":2,"transferability":2}},{"evidence_id":"EV078","decision":"exclude","span_ids":["S5","S6","S8"],"role":"generic photocatalysis background","claim":"PL lifetimes and transient photocurrent in a Zr-MOF system were interpreted as indicating charge separation and electron accumulation/transfer to active sites.","transfer_limit":"Different catalyst class and no cobalt-bipyridine donor comparison; interpretation-heavy and distant from target chemistry.","reason":"Although it discusses photophysical observables, it does not specifically inform the TEA/TEOA effect in Co(II)–bipyridine CO2 photoreduction as well as more relevant snippets do.","scores":{"research_relevance":1,"direct_evidence":2,"discriminatory_value":1,"transferability":1}},{"evidence_id":"EV079","decision":"include","span_ids":["S2","S3"],"role":"system option / comparative benchmark","claim":"A summary table reports a Co–Co LDH/Ti3C2 photocatalyst using MeCN/H2O/TEOA and [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2·6H2O under 5 W LED, with CO as reported product at 6.248 µmol/h.","transfer_limit":"This is a summarized table entry rather than a full primary report in the snippet, and the catalyst is a heterogeneous Co-based material, not a Co(II)–bipyridine molecular complex. CO denotes carbon monoxide product.","reason":"Useful as concise evidence that TEOA with Ru(bpy)3 and a cobalt-containing photocatalytic CO2 reduction system can yield CO under MeCN/H2O conditions, helping define alternative formulations and product-analysis scope.","scores":{"research_relevance":2,"direct_evidence":1,"discriminatory_value":1,"transferability":2}},{"evidence_id":"EV080","decision":"include","span_ids":["S3","S5","S6"],"role":"transferable operando assignment/control evidence","claim":"Operando XANES and isotope-labeled operando FTIR were used under reaction conditions to test structural assignments and vibrational assignments; replacing H2O with D2O shifted a peak to support assignment to a hydrogen-containing adsorbate.","transfer_limit":"Electrocatalytic Cu system for ethanol, not photocatalytic Co(II)–bipyridine; mechanistic species are different, so transfer is limited to the value of operando and isotopic assignment controls rather than specific chemistry.","reason":"Provides strong transferable evidence that operando spectroscopy plus isotope substitution can directly discriminate among competing assignments, which is valuable for designing controls in the target photocatalytic system.","scores":{"research_relevance":2,"direct_evidence":3,"discriminatory_value":3,"transferability":2}}]}
